item.title: Kellen Moore stands by decision to go for two at end of overtime vs. Lions
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: When the Saints scored a touchdown against the Lions with 1:34 remaining in overtime on Sunday, they could have kicked the extra point to tie the game, then hoped that either their defense could get the ball back so they could win, or at least hold the Lions' offense to preserve a tie.
item.content:encoded:
When the Saints scored a touchdown against the Lions with 1:34 remaining in overtime on Sunday, they could have kicked the extra point to tie the game, then hoped that either their defense could get the ball back so they could win, or at least hold the Lions' offense to preserve a tie. Instead, Saints head coach Kellen Moore decided to go for two, and end the game right there, one way or the other.

The way it ended was the Saints lost: Tyler Shough's two-point conversion pass was incomplete out the back of the end zone, and the Saints walked off the field 0-1. After the game, Moore said he thinks he made the right call.

"There was 1:34 left. That's a really talented offense. We had a chance to go win the football game," Moore said. "I really viewed it as we're going for two there to win the game, if we have a chance."

The Saints also decided to kick off at the start of overtime, thinking they'd rather get the ball second and know what they have to do. Deciding to kick at the start of overtime played into the decision to go for two at the end of overtime: Because the Saints had the second possession, Moore knew what his team had to do, and what his team had to do was score a two-point conversion. It didn't work, but Moore still thinks it was the right call.

item.title: Deshaun Watson says he'll "keep smiling, regardless of who's against me or who's with me"
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Watson seems likely to remain Cleveland's starting quarterback for at least another week.
item.content:encoded:
If you look at Deshaun Watson's final numbers from Cleveland's 34-10 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday, you might be able to talk yourself into some positives.

After all, Watson was 16-of-22 for 205 yards with a touchdown and an interception — good for 9.3 yards per attempt and a 97.7 passer rating.

But if you watched the game, you’d know 46 of those yards came on a garbage-time touchdown to Denzel Boston against the Jaguars’ backups. You would’ve seen Watson fire an interception to end Cleveland’s first drive, almost throw another to end the second, and then get strip-sacked on the third. You would understand that most — if not all — of Jacksonville’s five sacks on Watson happened because he was dropping so far back that the offensive line couldn’t form a cohesive pocket. You might’ve been baffled by how often he was trying to change a call at the line of scrimmage too late in the play clock.

Cleveland’s first drive had gotten off to a solid start, with the team moving the ball before Watson’s interception. After that, the unit was off the rails with no sense of rhythm.

But Watson said postgame that the pick didn’t rattle him.

“No, I mean, bad plays are going to happen all the time,” he said in his press conference. “You look all around the league. Everyone throws interceptions, everyone makes bad plays. You've got to give the defense credit. He made a good play on that. Even though I got knocked off my platform a little bit, I thought I got it over him. He reached up and grabbed it. So you've got to move on to the next play and try to move forward and try to put something positive on the next drive. And we weren't able to do that.

“So it didn't really bundle up my confidence. It's just — we didn't get back on track like we wanted to.”

Will the Browns’ dalliance with Watson continue? It seems likely, for at least another week. And so, Watson will lean on his experience in dealing with adversity as the Browns ready to play the Buccaneers.

“Yeah, I mean just keep moving forward, keep stepping forward, keep smiling, regardless of who's against me or who's with me,” Watson said. “I think that's more beneficial for the team in that locker room. I've had a lot of support in that locker room after the game telling me to keep my head up, keep pushing forward, keep working. They're behind me, so that's always positive to see and hear. Yeah, we just got to keep going.

“The adversity is going to be there. You've got to embrace it. That's the only way — I thought it was going to be gone two years ago, but I guess not. So you just embrace it and keep pushing through until you break that wall through.”

The Browns will be on the road to face Baker Mayfield and the Bucs next Sunday.

item.title: CBS announces next two weeks of broadcasters, with no Tony Romo
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: CBS has said nothing more about the status of No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo since CBS placed him on leave, with a one-sentence press release.
item.content:encoded:
CBS has said nothing more about the status of No. 1 NFL analyst Tony Romo since CBS placed him on leave, with a one-sentence press release.

On Monday, CBS confirmed that Romo's leave won't be ending before Week 4.

CBS has announced the broadcast teams for Week 2 and Week 3. The top team continues to consist of Jim Nantz and J.J. Watt. That includes the Ravens-Cowboys game to be played in Brazil.

Most believe Romo won't return this year. Many believe he'll never be back, with only a buyout to be negotiated.

After Romo issued a statement on September 1 disclosing that he would be pleading no-contest to charges related to an OWI arrest in Milwaukee, CBS had nothing to say. Which said plenty.

There may never be a statement in which CBS declares that its relationship with Romo is over. The message may simply come one development at a time, starting with Watt replacing him for Week 1 — and continuing with Watt keeping the spot for Week 2 and Week 3.

item.title: Report: Falcons DL Da'Shawn Hand believed to have a torn quad
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Falcons opened the 2026 season with a loss to the Steelers and they may have lost a defensive lineman for the rest of the year as well.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons opened the 2026 season with a loss to the Steelers and they may have lost a defensive lineman for the rest of the year as well.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand is believed to have a torn quad that would require season-ending surgery. Hand is soliciting other opinions before making a decision about a course of action.

Hand signed a one-year deal with the Falcons this offseason. He played seven snaps on Sunday before leaving with his injury.

The Falcons have already lost linebacker Jalon Walker for the season and James Pearce has seven games to go on his suspension, so the front seven is getting thin in Atlanta.

item.title: Will Anderson is now the betting favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Rams defensive end Myles Garrett entered the season as the clear favorite to win the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year award.
item.content:encoded:
Rams defensive end Myles Garrett entered the season as the clear favorite to win the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year award. That didn't last long.

Garrett did nothing in Week 1, and is now out through at least Week 5 with a knee injury, and his odds to win Defensive Player of the Year have dropped to +2500. And now there's a new favorite.

Texans defensive end Will Anderson is now favored to win the award, with +320 odds. Anderson and the Texans' defense did not have a great game in Sunday's 36-31 loss to the Bills, but Anderson is one of the best pass rushers in the league, and Defensive Player of the Year usually goes to a great pass rusher.

Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, who had two sacks in a Week 1 win over the Saints, is second in Defensive Player of the Year odds at +500. He's followed by Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt (+650), who had a tremendous pick-six in Sunday's win over the Falcons, and Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby (+900), who had 1.5 sacks in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins.

item.title: Derrick Henry, Lamar Jackson star in win over Colts
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Henry ran for three touchdowns in a 41-23 Ravens win.
item.content:encoded:
The Jesse Minter era in Baltimore got off to a winning start.

One of Minter's first big moves was hiring Declan Doyle as his offensive coordinator and that decision paid off for the Ravens' biggest stars in their season-opening win over the Colts. Derrick Henry ran for 144 yards and three touchdowns, Lamar Jackson produced a pair of touchdowns and the Ravens will head into Week 2 off the back of a 41-23 win.

Jackson finished 17-of-25 for 324 yards through the air and he ran four times for 43 yards in the kind of performance that the Ravens saw far too infrequently while missing the playoffs last year. He opened the scoring with a touchdown run that he set up with a 49-yard strike to wide receiver Zay Flowers and later hooked up with Flowers for a 52-yard score.

Flowers had five catches for 150 yards in less than two quarters, but then missed the rest of the game with a hamstring injury. The Ravens also lost wideout Ja'Kobi Lane to a wrist injury, which gives them a pair of concerns at the position as they get set to host the Saints in Week 2.

The Ravens fell down 6-0 to open the game, but quickly took the lead with a pair of touchdowns wrapped around a Roquan Smith interception of Colts quarterback Daniel Jones. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey forced another turnover by stripping Jonathan Taylor and the Ravens were up 28-6 at one point in the first half.

The final score got more respectable as the Ravens slowed down in the wake of Flowers's injury, but the overall picture is one that will make for a lot of smiles around the team's facility this week.

Jones finished 19-of-31 for 166 yards in his first game since tearing his Achilles last season. He only ran once, which is a big difference from how he was used prior to the injury and that missing dimension didn't help the Colts' cause on Sunday. Their defense's inability to stop the Ravens hurt them more, though, and they'll have to try to come up with something better on both sides of the ball to avoid an 0-2 start when they head to Kansas City next week.

item.title: Lions choke away 21-0 lead, survive to beat Saints 31-30 in overtime
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: In a wild Week 1 battle, the Saints nearly completed an epic comeback, but couldn't convert their two-point attempt in overtime.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions and Saints played an epic Week 1 game that couldn't be decided in 60 minutes, but after each team scored an overtime touchdown, Detroit ultimately prevailed.

Saints quarterback Tyler Shough's two-point conversion pass was incomplete out the back of the end zone on the final play of overtime, and the Lions survived 31-30.

For most of the game, it looked like the Lions would win easily: Detroit led 21-0 in the third quarter and seemed poised to cruise to an easy win. Instead, the Lions choked the lead away and easily could have lost in regulation: Saints kicker Daniel Carlson lined up for a game-winning field goal as time expired in the fourth quarter, but his 62-yard attempt missed.

There were some positives for the Lions: Jahmyr Gibbs, whom the Lions made the highest-paid running back in the NFL last month, delivered in a big way, with 156 yards rushing and two touchdowns. And Aidan Hutchinson sacked Shough twice. But for the Lions, the big question coming out of the game is why they couldn't put the Saints away when they should have.

For the Saints, it was a heartbreaking loss but a sign that Shough is starting to grow within Kellen Moore's offense. The heavily favored Lions won, but the Saints have to feel good about the way they fought until the end.

item.title: Bengals recover four Bucs fumbles, hold on to win 33-27
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Bengals had a makeover of their defense in the offseason after ranking 31st in yards and 30th in points last season.
item.content:encoded:
The Bengals had a makeover of their defense in the offseason after ranking 31st in yards and 30th in points last season. They showed off their new look on Sunday.

The Bengals allowed only 282 yards, forced four fumbles they recovered and had four sacks in a 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.

Bucs quarterback Baker Mayfield lost three fumbles — one that Bengals linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. returned 27 yards for a touchdown and another into the end zone that safety Bryan Cook recovered. Running back Bucky Irving also lost a fumble.

Still, Mayfield gave the Bucs a chance with a 9-yard touchdown run with 3:19 left. Joe Burrow, though, drove the Bengals 54 yards in eight plays, allowing the clock to expire on Tampa Bay's comeback.

Burrow went 25-of-35 for 254 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Bucs rookie Josiah Trotter intercepted Burrow on a third-and-5 pass intended for Andrei Iosivas and returned it 38 yards for a touchdown.

Burrow's touchdown was a 2-yard throw to tight end Mike Gesicki, who had five catches for 78 yards. Ja'Marr Chase had only two catches for 12 yards.

Evan McPherson kicked field goals of 20, 55, 58 and 32 yards.

item.title: Myles Garrett will have knee surgery, head to IR
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The dream team has encountered an unexpected detour.
item.content:encoded:
The dream team has had an unexpected detour.

After losing to the 49ers badly in Melbourne, and given Myles Garrett's candid remarks about the impact of his health on his performance, Garrett will have knee surgery and be placed on injured reserve, per multiple reports.

It's a stunning development for a Rams team that became the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl after Garrett's arrival in June. His presence lured Aaron Donald out of retirement. Now, Donald will be playing for at least four games (if Donald plays in Week 2) without Garrett.

And it won't be an easy road. The Rams host the Giants next Monday night. The following Sunday night, they face the Broncos in Denver. Then, the Rams head to Philly for a date with the Eagles. After that, the Rams return home for a Monday night showdown with Josh Allen and the Bills.

item.title: Bears beat Panthers 59-37 in Week 1 offensive frenzy
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Plenty of points were scored as Chicago went to Carolina and won a fun one in Week One.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears' and Panthers' offenses ran wild today in Carolina, but the Bears were wilder.

Chicago had an incredible game running the ball, with a total of 39 carries for 291 yards and six rushing touchdowns, and Caleb Williams added 269 passing yards and two more touchdowns, in a 59-37 win.

The Panthers' offense played well too, with Bryce Young passing for 361 yards and three touchdowns and adding a rushing touchdown. If the Panthers' defense could have stopped anyone, Young and the Panthers' offense could have been the talk of the league in Week 1.

But the Panthers' defense couldn't stop the Bears, who ran the ball almost at will. (The one exception was a surprising fourth-and-1 attempt from the Bears' own 21-yard line that went nowhere.) It was a tremendous showing from coach Ben Johnson's offense.

The Bears were one of the surprises of the NFL last season, winning the NFC North when few thought they could. This year they look like they're going to be a tough team to beat again.

item.title: Bears-Panthers was highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bears and Panthers made some history on Sunday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The Bears and Panthers made some history on Sunday afternoon.

Chicago's 59-37 road win was the highest-scoring Week 1 game in NFL history. The previous record was 88 points, which came in a 48-40 Buccaneers win over the Saints during the 2018 season.

It was also the first time that any NFL game ended in a 59-37 score. The 96 points were also the most total points in a game for both the Bears and the Panthers and it was the highest-scoring game in the NFL since the Rams and Chiefs combined for 105 points in a 2018 game.

It was not the most points that the Bears have ever scored in a game. They put up 61 points in regular season games during the 1965 and 1980 seasons and they scored 73 points in the 1940 NFL championship game.

item.title: Broncos have no injury designations for Monday night
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Denver Broncos' shot at an appearance in Super Bowl LX arguably was derailed by an injury to quarterback Bo Nix.
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos' shot at an appearance in Super Bowl LX arguably was derailed by an injury to quarterback Bo Nix. As the 2026 season begins, Nix and the rest of the team are healthy.

Denver has no injury designations in advance of the Monday night opener against the Chiefs in Kansas City.

Only receiver Marvin Mims appeared on the Week 1 injury report. He fully participated in practice on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday with a foot injury.

No team will be much healthier than it is in Week 1. The Broncos are good to go, as they try to win the AFC West for the second straight year. The extent to which they can stay that way will be a major factor in whether they can get back to the Super Bowl for the first time since 2015.

item.title: Robert Saleh: Cam Ward has all the tools, but it's a long process
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Titans quarterback Cam Ward said he was disappointed with how he and the team played in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets and he's sure to find plenty of people willing to co-sign that assessment of their first game under head coach Robert Saleh.
item.content:encoded:
Titans quarterback Cam Ward said he was disappointed with how he and the team played in Sunday's 23-10 loss to the Jets and he's sure to find plenty of people willing to co-sign that assessment of their first game under head coach Robert Saleh.

Some people might go a little further than disappointed when it comes to where the first overall pick of the 2025 draft is as he starts his second NFL season. Ward's best moments of the game came on a drive with under five minutes to play and the Titans down big, which led to Saleh being asked at a Monday press conference if the quarterback is more of a work in progress than the staff thought when they got to Tennessee.

Saleh pointed out that Ward has had seven offensive coordinators in the last seven years and that they are "trying to build a foundation" for him to make the needed improvements.

"His growth will happen throughout the year," Saleh said. "His growth is gonna happen next year and the year after. This young man is at the floor of what it takes to be an NFL quarterback, but he has all the tools, the mental makeup to get to where he needs to go. It’s time on task, it’s giving the kid stability, it’s giving the young man the chance to be repetitive in his day-to-day process with the right coaching to help him get better. . . . It's a long process, long process to get these kids to get them where you need to get to, quarterback especially."

Saleh said he's not trying to "shield" Ward and noted both some "easy throws" that he thinks the quarterback would want to have back and improvements he's seen in Ward's pocket presence. Signs of those gains are going to have to start coming a little more often if Ward is going to continue looking like a worthwhile project in Tennessee.

item.title: Jahmyr Gibbs had career-high 29 carries, and Dan Campbell says he can do even more
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had a career-high 29 carries for 156 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday, and he added five catches for 30 yards.
item.content:encoded:
Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs had a career-high 29 carries for 156 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday, and he added five catches for 30 yards. That's an enormous workload for any player, but Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game that Gibbs could do even more.

"I thought it was a very promising Week 1," Campbell said. "Certainly, we know what Gibbs is, what he's capable of, and he's still not there yet. And I mean that in a good way."

What more could Gibbs do? Campbell said that on a day when Gibbs' longest run was 21 yards, he's capable of breaking some much longer runs than that.

"We were this close to breaking three or four more of these, breaking them wide open," Campbell said. "A shoestring away, just a little longer block at the second level. I mean, we were close, and we're going to get that cleaned up, and he's going to get better. Week 1, yeah, I like where he's at. I'm glad he's here."

Campbell is not looking for Gibbs to get 29 carries a game for 17 games. That would be 493 carries for the season, which would be the second-most in NFL history. But Campbell said he's happy to keep feeding Gibbs the rock.

"Do I want to set records with how many carries? No, that's not something I want to do, but when you look at a guy and you think he's in good shape, he had a really good camp, he's in the best shape I've seen since I've been here," Campbell said.

Gibbs will have to be in good shape for the workload the Lions are giving him.

item.title: Bills score late, then stop Texans to win 36-31 in classic
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Josh Allen, who was 0-4 in Houston, threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Josh Palmer with 1:36 remaining.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills and Texans put on a show on Sunday afternoon. There may not be many games this season that are better than the season opener in Houston.

Josh Allen, who was 0-4 in Houston, threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Josh Palmer with 1:36 remaining for a 36-31 lead and then had to watch from the bench as the Bills held on.

The Texans had first-and-goal at the Buffalo 9 with 25 seconds left, but Deone Walker sacked C.J. Stroud for a 9-yard loss. After an incompletion, Greg Rousseau had a strip-sack of Stroud that Terrell Bernard recovered with 9 ticks left to end it.

The back-and-forth game had nine lead changes.

Allen ripped apart the Texans' vaunted defense, throwing for 334 yards and two touchdowns as the Bills had 409 total yards. He nearly threw his only interception on the play before the game-winner, but Kamari Lassiter, who had a rough day, dropped the pick in the end zone.

Tight end Dalton Kincaid caught five passes for 130 yards and DJ Moore had five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown in his Buffalo debut.

James Cook ran for 57 yards on 13 carries.

The Texans gained 381 yards, but Stroud had the only two turnovers. He also lost a fumble on a strip-sack by Rousseau in the first half. Stroud finished 26-of-38 for 274 yards and two touchdowns.

The Texans showcased their free agent acquisition, David Montgomery, as he had 20 carries for 60 yards and two touchdowns and three catches for 19 yards and a touchdown. The Texans had 32 rushes and 38 passes, held the ball for 36:17 and went 2-for-2 on fourth down.

item.title: Packers melt down in fourth quarter, Vikings pull off 39-22 victory
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Despite losing Kyler Murray in the first quarter, Minnesota pulled off a stunning win with a huge fourth quarter.
item.content:encoded:
Early in the fourth quarter, armed with a 22-17 lead over Minnesota, Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur made a couple of decisions.

The result of those choices proved to be disastrous and allowed the Vikings to come away with a 39-22 victory to open the 2026 season.

On fourth-and-6 from Minnesota’s 22-yard line, Packers rookie Trey Smack hit a 40-yard field goal to give Green Bay an eight-point, 25-17 lead. But the Vikings were flagged for an offside penalty.

That induced LaFleur’s first choice — taking the field goal off the board to go for it on fourth-and-1.

The second choice was LaFleur’s play call: A QB sneak.

But quarterback Jordan Love failed to convert, with a virtual measurement confirming Love was short of the sticks.

Now with Green Bay holding just a five-point lead, the Vikings got down the field due to a cacophony of errors from Green Bay’s defense. It looked like the Packers would get off the field on third-and-11 with a sack of Carson Wentz, but Green Bay was flagged for illegal contact for a free first down.

On the next set of downs, when Wentz just avoided a sack by getting rid of the ball on third-and-3, Chris McClellan was flagged for a questionable roughing-the-passer penalty, as he braced himself before falling on Wentz with his full body weight.

Then when Wentz was intercepted by safety Evan Williams in the end zone, the Packers got flagged for defensive holding, giving the Vikings another free first down.

Finally, Aaron Jones ran it in against his old team for a 3-yard touchdown.

It got worse — or better, depending on your perspective — from there. Love was sacked twice in a row on the ensuing drive, with the ball coming out on the second. The Vikings started their next drive from the 1-yard line, with Jordan Mason powering it in for a touchdown on the first play.

And then Love tossed the first interception of his career at U.S. Bank Stadium, with the ball getting tipped at the line before going off of Harrison Smith’s hands and into the waiting arms of James Pierre.

Justin Jefferson caught his second touchdown of the game to finish that drive, giving the Vikings a stunning 17-point lead.

The Packers had led 22-10 in the third quarter and were outscored 29-0 for the rest of the game, including 22-0 in the fourth quarter.

It was a remarkable victory for the Vikings, who lost their starting quarterback on their third possession. Kyler Murray was hit hard in the head while sliding on a third down. The Packers were flagged for unnecessary roughness while Murray went straight to the locker room for further examination and was diagnosed with a concussion.

So Wentz came in and managed the game well, finishing 12-of-19 for 133 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Two of his TD passes went to Justin Jefferson, who hadn’t caught a score at home since 2024. The wideout finished with eight catches for 92 yards with two TDs.

On the other side, things were going very well for the Packers before the ill-fated QB sneak. Love finished the contest 21-of-42 for 387 yards with two touchdowns and a pick. Christian Watson had six catches for 147 yards with two TDs, but five of those receptions and 131 of those yards came in the first half.

Now at 1-0, the Vikings will be on the road for another divisional game against the 1-0 Bears next week.

The 0-1 Packers, who now have a disturbing trend of blowing significant leads, will again be on the road to face the 1-0 Jets.

item.title: Cardinals beat Chargers in NFL's biggest upset of Week 1
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: The Chargers were the NFL's biggest favorites, with a 9.5-point spread. Instead, the Cardinals won 26-14.
item.content:encoded:
The Chargers were 9.5-point favorites against the Cardinals today in Los Angeles, the biggest betting line in the NFL for Week 1. No one thought this was a game Arizona would win.

But that's why they play the games.

In a major upset that may force us to reassess what we thought we knew about both teams, the Cardinals went to Los Angeles and beat the Chargers 26-14.

First-year Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur deserves an enormous amount of credit for having his team ready to play, and Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh will face plenty of questions about why his team wasn't. Harbaugh had previously been 6-0 in Week 1 in his NFL coaching career.

Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett played well, completing 27 of 37 passes for 277 yards, with one touchdown and no interceptions. His favorite receiver was Trey McBride, who caught nine passes for 95 yards and a touchdown. The Cardinals surprisingly made Tyler Allgeier, not rookie Jeremiyah Love, their primary ball carrier.

Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert turned in a highly disappointing performance, completing 17 of 27 passes for 209 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. And the Chargers' running game never got going. Also alarming for the Chargers is that wide receiver Ladd McConkey suffered a chest injury late in the game and went to the locker room.

The Cardinals also had a concerning injury when safety Kitan Crawford was carted off during the fourth quarter, but today was mostly great news in Arizona: This team looks better than anyone thought.

item.title: Malik Nabers knew it was time to make his return during pregame warmups
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Wide receiver Malik Nabers made his first appearance in the Giants' lineup in almost a year when he took the field against the Cowboys on Sunday night.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Malik Nabers made his first appearance in the Giants' lineup in almost a year when he took the field against the Cowboys on Sunday night.

Nabers tore his ACL last September and he remained noncommittal about playing all the way through the week. After the 28-20 win, Nabers said he was up in the air all the way through pregame warmups and that he told his family not to come to the game because he didn't want to disappoint them by not playing.

"The deciding factor was just when I got out there, I just felt good," Nabers said after the game. "I felt good. I got a little chill through my body and I was like, "Yeah, it's time. It's time."

Quarterback Jaxson Dart said in his press conference that head coach John Harbaugh tackled Nabers during a walkthrough earlier in the weekend to show the wideout that he was ready. It took a little longer for Nabers to be convinced, but Dart was happy that the outcome allowed him to throw the ball to his top target.

"It was great, it was great. He's just a guy where, no matter what the coverage is, no matter who they put out there on him, you have all the confidence in the world that he's going to make a play," Dart said.

Nabers finished the day with six catches for 69 yards and the Giants will be looking for even bigger numbers now that he's got the first game back under his belt.

item.title: Sunday Night Football: Jaxson Dart throws three TDs, Giants beat Cowboys 28-20
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: New York won its first game under new head coach John Harbaugh by controlling the ball and the clock.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants certainly looked like a new squad under new head coach John Harbaugh.

New York used long, punishing drives to control the game, defeating Dallas 28-20 on Sunday Night Football.

After a Dak Prescott interception late in the second quarter, the Giants took a 14-7 lead into halftime with Isaiah Likely’s 15-yard touchdown catch from quarterback Jaxson Dart. Then, after receiving the second-half kickoff, Likely scored his second touchdown to cap a 12-play, 74-yard drive that took 8:01 off the clock, pushing the lead to 21-7.

The Cowboys responded with a long touchdown drive of their own. But the Giants effectively put the game out of reach with another long drive featuring several swing passes — including Dart’s 9-yard TD pass to Devin Singletary.

That drive took 8:11 off the clock, leaving just 7:26 in the final period.

Dallas again scored, this time on a 17-yard reception from Javonte Williams. But the running back taunted as he crossed the goal line, resulting in a 15-yard penalty. Brandon Aubrey missed the extra point wide right, keeping it an eight-point game.

But even with an extra point — or a potential two-point conversion — it wouldn’t have mattered, because the Cowboys defense could not get a stop. Dallas never got the ball back, as the Giants held it for the last 5:21 to win.

New York ended the game with 29 first downs, 394 yards, and was 9-of-11 on third down. The club was really 9-of-10, as the final third down was a knee from Dart to run out the clock.

The Giants’ second-year QB was 23-of-29 for 230 yards with three touchdowns and no picks. He also had 54 yards on the ground.

Likely was his top target throughout the night, catching all eight of his targets for 78 yards with his two TDs. Malik Nabers — returning from a torn ACL — caught six passes for 69 yards. Cam Skattebo had 81 yards on 18 carries with a TD.

On the other side, Prescott finished 22-of-34 for 175 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. There wasn’t much running room, as Williams finished with just 41 yards on 12 carries. CeeDee Lamb was limited to 44 yards on five catches with a touchdown. George Pickens had a bad drop down the sideline in the first half, finishing with just three catches for 28 yards.

Dallas may have some more issues defensively, as the team lost a couple of key players. Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown went down in the fourth quarter with a hamstring injury. Malik Hooker also had to exit with a forearm injury in the second half and was not able to return.

Now at 1-0, the Giants will be on the road next week to play the Rams on Monday night.

The 0-1 Cowboys will have their home opener next Sunday afternoon against the Commanders.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor: Loss to Ravens definitely a wakeup call
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Colts picked up right where they left off in Week 1 of the 2026 season, but that was not a good thing.
item.content:encoded:
The Colts picked up right where they left off in Week 1 of the 2026 season, but that was not a good thing.

Indianapolis lost their final seven games last year and they are 0-1 after giving up 506 yards and turning the ball over twice in a 41-23 home loss to the Ravens on Sunday. The Colts only managed 251 yards of their own and running back Jonathan Taylor said after the game that he hopes the beating serves as a reminder that its time for the team to start taking things seriously.

"Definitely an eye-opener, definitely a wakeup call," Taylor said, via the team's website. "Like, hey, season's here. Obviously we know no one's gonna give us anything, but it's a good team over there and it's like, hey, doesn't matter what you guys did last year, you gotta prove it again this year."

Taylor ran for 98 yards and two scores, but the rest of the offense was underwhelming in quarterback Daniel Jones's return from a torn Achilles. They'll have to hope that more time back on the field helps Jones get back to where he was early last season because more of the same in the weeks to come is going to make for a long season in Indianapolis.

item.title: Jim Harbaugh: We were too sloppy
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Sunday night saw John Harbaugh win his first game as the head coach of the Giants, but it wasn't a great day for the whole Harbaugh family.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday night saw John Harbaugh win his first game as the head coach of the Giants, but it wasn't a great day for the whole Harbaugh family.

Jim Harbaugh's Chargers came into Week 1 as the biggest favorite in the league, but anyone who backed them at home over the Cardinals went home a little poorer. The Cardinals never trailed and shut the Chargers out in the fourth quarter of a 26-14 win that left Harbaugh to say that "quite a few things" went wrong for his team.

“Some uncharacteristic things happened. Give them credit for making them happen,” Harbaugh said at his press conference. “I would call it sloppy at times. Too sloppy. That’s something we need to get fixed.”

Harbaugh cited seven penalties, but there were also two turnovers, a blocked punt and the offense failing to convert multiple times on fourth downs. The offense was limited to 268 yards overall, which didn't fit with the enthusiastic praise that Harbaugh lavished on quarterback Justin Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel throughout the offseason.

That duo will have more chances to get things right, but the first look at this year's Chargers looked a lot like the last glimpse of the 2025 version and that's not where anyone with the team hoped to find themselves.

item.title: Jaxson Dart: Identity starts at the top and we bought into John Harbaugh's plan
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Giants capped the first Sunday of the 2026 season with their first win under head coach John Harbaugh.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants capped the first Sunday of the 2026 season with their first win under head coach John Harbaugh.

Dallas was the favorite at MetLife Stadium, but the Giants drove for a touchdown the first time they had the ball and never trailed on their way to a 28-20 win that featured plenty to like in every phase of the game. Quarterback Jaxson Dart threw three touchdowns and ran for 54 yards while showing full command of the offense to kick off his second season, and said after the game that the effort was a result of putting everything Harbaugh has been preaching into action.

"I just think that we have so much respect for coach Harbs, and this team will do whatever he says because we have all the faith that he's going to put us in the best situation to win," Dart said. "The identity of a team starts at the top and it starts with how he's conducted himself, with how he's created a tough team. We want to take that on our shoulders and we bought in to what his plan is week in and week out. We're definitely happy to get it for him. We were just really happy to get it — not only for the players but for the organization."

It's the first time the Giants opened a season with a win since 2022, which was the last time that they ended a season with a trip to the playoffs. Sunday night's performance will have some around the team thinking about a similar destination and it will be on Harbaugh to make sure that no one gets too far ahead of themselves after a stirring debut.

item.title: DeMeco Ryans: C.J. Stroud played well enough for us to win
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: C.J.
item.content:encoded:
C.J. Stroud threw for 274 yards and two touchdowns. He had a 106.7 passer rating.

The Texans quarterback also lost two fumbles on strip sacks by Greg Rousseau, and the Bills won 36-31 as Stroud couldn't get them in the end zone despite a first-and-goal at the 9.

Coach DeMeco Ryans thought Stroud played well enough to win, pointing to the 409 yards his vaunted defense gave up. That included 334 passing yards by Josh Allen.

“C.J. was very much in control the entire game," Ryans said, via texanscommenter. "Took what the defense gave him. Made great decisions with the football. Proud of the way he played today. He showed what he’s been showing all camp, that confidence, that growth. Was very calm, great demeanor, putting us in a great position to win the game.

"Unfortunately, we lost the football there two times. Don’t want those plays at all, but not going to let that overshadow the game that he had. Offense put up way more points than needed for us to win this game. Could’ve definitely played much better defensively.”

The Texans had first-and-goal at the Buffalo 9 with 25 seconds left, but Deone Walker sacked Stroud for a 9-yard loss. After an incompletion, Rousseau had a strip-sack of Stroud that Terrell Bernard recovered with 9 ticks left to end it.

“Got down there," Stroud said. "Can’t get stalemated like that. That sack kind of made it tougher, but even then, we still had a chance. I’m trying my best to protect the ball but also to make plays. We needed seven right there, so I can’t be super conservative. I've got to be able to take shots. Sometimes it doesn’t roll your way. We’ll try to fix that and go forward.”

item.title: Jalen Hurts: It's about meeting the moment when opportunity comes
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: There were some long stretches during Sunday's game when the Eagles offense failed to click, including five three-and-outs in 11 total possessions, but they were able to beat the Commanders because of big plays that got sprinkled throughout the contest.
item.content:encoded:
There were some long stretches during Sunday's game when the Eagles offense failed to click, including five three-and-outs in 11 total possessions, but they were able to beat the Commanders because of big plays that got sprinkled throughout the contest.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts had a hand in many of them. He hit a 64-yard pass to wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks to set up tight end Dallas Goedert's first touchdown catch and then hit Wicks for another score later in the first half. After the Commanders cut the Eagles' lead to one point in the fourth quarter, Hurts scrambled for 22 yards on third-and-18 and then hit Goedert for a 43-yard score that gave them the cushion they needed to finish out a 24-22 victory.

After the game, Hurts was asked about his ability to come up with big plays when his team needs them the most.

“Yeah, but it's not something that's forced," Hurts said, via a transcript from the team. "It's the same focus that you have throughout the whole entire game. It's the same poise that you play with throughout the whole entire game. And so, it goes back to all 11 being on the same page and then me taking responsibility and the opportunities I have with the ball in my hand. Talking about this on a production meeting leading up to the game with [Tom] Brady. When you're playing a position, a lot of it is about making sure you're in the right play, when you're doing the right thing that takes no talent. . . . It’s just about meeting the moment when your opportunity comes. Collectively, we’ve got a lot to build on, obviously a lot to correct and I'm excited to get back into the process of becoming the team that we're supposed to become.”

Putting together a steadier and more consistent offensive attack will be on the list of things to correct as the Eagles move into Week 2 and beyond, but that process will be made easier thanks to the knowledge that they can turn to Hurts and expect him to come up with something special in the biggest moments of games.

item.title: Josh Allen on late TD to beat Texans: Sometimes the ball bounces your way
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: It's hard to come up with too many examples of how thin the line between winning and losing can be than back-to-back plays that the Bills ran late in the fourth quarter in Houston on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
It's hard to come up with too many examples of how thin the line between winning and losing can be than back-to-back plays that the Bills ran late in the fourth quarter in Houston on Sunday.

On a second down from the Texans' 34-yard-line with just under two minutes to play and the Bills down one, quarterback Josh Allen chucked a pass into the end zone and Texans cornerback Kamari Lassiter was the only player in position to catch it. Lassiter was unable to make the interception while stumbling backward, however, and Allen got another chance. He made good on it with a perfect strike to Josh Palmer for the game-winning touchdown.

"Hey, it's football. What can I say? Sometimes the ball bounces your way," Allen said in his postgame press conference.

Allen was 0-4 in previous trips to Houston and the Bills had not won there since 2006. That stretch included Allen taking eight sacks in a loss last season, but the Bills only allowed two this time and Allen had enough time to average 11.5 yards per attempt. That and a little good fortune made all the difference for the Bills on this trip to Texas.

item.title: Travis Hunter played 4 snaps on offense, 29 on defense
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter was a starter on defense and a bit player on offense in Week 1 against the Browns.
item.content:encoded:
Jaguars cornerback and wide receiver Travis Hunter was a starter on defense and a bit player on offense in Week 1 against the Browns.

Hunter played 29 snaps on defense, which was 57 percent of the Jaguars' defensive plays, and four snaps on offense, or 7 percent. Hunter did not play at all on special teams.

The Jaguars tried to get Hunter the ball when he was on the field on offense, and he got one carry for three yards and one catch for eight yards. On defense, he had one tackle.

When the Jaguars drafted Hunter last year, they thought he could be the NFL's only full-time starter on both offense and defense. So far in his NFL career, it hasn't worked out that way. As a rookie last year he had played 67 percent of offensive snaps and 36 percent of defensive snaps when an injury ended his season after seven games, and the early indications this year are that he won't be a regular contributor on offense.

Hunter is contributing, but not enough to live up to the hype surrounding his status as last year's second overall pick.

item.title: Zac Taylor: We felt the presence of our defensive additions on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The biggest storyline of the Bengals offseason was the moves they made to improve their defense and the new players were front and center in Sunday's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
item.content:encoded:
The biggest storyline of the Bengals offseason was the moves they made to improve their defense and the new players were front and center in Sunday's 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.

Defensive end Boye Mafe had a sack, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery while safety Bryan Cook also forced and recovered a fumble. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen had a sack and the defense forced four turnovers while sacking Baker Mayfield four times overall.

After the game, head coach Zac Taylor said the team "felt their presence" when asked about the new faces but holdover linebacker Barrett Carter shrugged off any suggestion that the performance validated anything to the team as a whole.

"We haven't answered any questions," Carter said, via a transcript from the team. "Like I said, this what we expected. We haven't answered any questions. The Bengals are 1-0, we had four turnovers — that's great — but we should have won by much more. I don't mean that against the Buccaneers, but we need to dominate teams, so there's a lot more plays to be made. This defensive team, we have not done anything. We have not even scratched the surface. There's a lot more plays to be made."

The key for the Bengals will now be to use Sunday's effort as a foundation for the continued defensive growth they will need to end their playoff drought. The next test of that will come in Houston in Week 2.

item.title: Ashton Jeanty: We're building a new culture that's going to win games
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When the Raiders took running back Ashton Jeanty at the top of the first round in 2025, they had performances like Sunday's in mind.
item.content:encoded:
When the Raiders took running back Ashton Jeanty at the top of the first round in 2025, they had performances like Sunday's in mind.

Jeanty ran 23 times for 102 yards and caught a pair of touchdowns in a 27-13 win over the Dolphins. That came after Jeanty missed extended time this summer with an ankle injury, but he showed no signs of it on Sunday and the Raiders showed no signs of being the overmatched team that went 3-14 last season.

“The past is the past,” Jeanty said in a postgame press conference. “We’re moving forward, and we’re not worried about what happened last year. This is a new team, new staff, and we’re building a new culture here. And that’s a culture that’s going to win football games.”

There was a lot of talk about the Raiders turning the corner when they beat the Patriots in Week 1 under Pete Carroll last year, but they promptly went on a four-game losing streak that was much more indicative of how the year would play out. Klint Kubiak's charge will be making sure that the positives against Miami remain in place and riding Jeanty like they did on Sunday will likely be part of that plan.

item.title: Quarterback adversity has sparked growth for Kevin O'Connell
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As high-end analytics go, the Vikings make the playoffs every other year.
item.content:encoded:
As high-end analytics go, the Vikings make the playoffs every other year. At an even more complex mathematical level, the Vikings make the playoffs when the same quarterback starts and plays every game of the regular season.

Consequently, coach Kevin O'Connell had a simple goal for 2026: make it more like 2022 and 2024, when Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold, respectively, went wire-to-wire at the most important position on the field.

That plan went out the window on the third drive of the season, when quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a concussion.

Carson Wentz entered. It wasn't perfect. It wasn't pretty. They trailed with roughly 20 minutes to play, 22-10. In the fourth quarter, the dam broke — thanks to the defense.

After the game, O'Connell admitted that he has struggled in the past to overcome the unexpected issues of offense. He has now learned how to roll with the changes.

“Two of our years here, we've had our starting quarterback for essentially the whole season, and we won 14 and 13 games," O'Connell told reporters after the game. "In some of the adversity, I don't think I've coached very well. Trying to maybe worry about the stat sheet, worry about what it's gonna look like when you pick up the paper."

He's now realizing that the only stat that matters is points scored versus points allowed. And he benefits from a defensive coordinator in Brian Flores, who has a plan for creating the kind of chaos that can pick up the slack for the offense.

The message became clear last year, when the Vikings ran the table for five straight wins after the playoff pursuit was essentially lost. This year, with the quarterback questions starting earlier than ever for O'Connell, he is putting the lesson into action.

With or without Murray, it'll get tested next Sunday at Chicago.

item.title: Jaelan Phillips: Giving up 59 points is embarrassing, creates critical moment for Panthers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The good news for the Panthers was that they put 37 points on the board in their first game of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
The good news for the Panthers was that they put 37 points on the board in their first game of the 2026 season.

Sunday's bad news was that still left them 22 points behind their opposition. The Bears offense tore the Panthers defense apart in a 59-37 win that went down as the highest-scoring Week 1 game in the history of the NFL.

After the game, linebacker Jaelan Phillips was asked if he found himself looking at the scoreboard trying to make sense of what he saw.

"Many times, yeah, especially towards the end," Phillips said, via the team's website. "I mean, 59 is an ugly, ugly score to put up as a defense, so it's embarrassing. But at the end of the day, you know, I do think that it's a good opportunity for us. It's a critical moment in the sense that, you know, getting beat this badly as a defense is really going to define us moving forward in terms of the urgency that we have to make corrections and to get better, so you know it's all good, man."

The Panthers gave up the most points in league history during the 2024 season, but stuck with defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and improved last year. Bringing in Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd was designed to continue that improvement.

Sunday was a major step back and head coach Dave Canales said in his press conference that the team needs to "find solutions for what's going on" because more of the same is going to make for a long, ugly season for Carolina.
